quotes.text: Co-pilot doesn't create order. It consumes whatever order you already have. And if what you have is entropy, co-pilot operationalizes entropy at conversational speed.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why Copilot quality mirrors the state of the tenant rather than the model.

quotes.text: Data is not context. Data is raw material. Context is curated, permission correct, relationship aware, time valid material, assembled for a decision.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A precise, architect-level distinction between data and context.

quotes.text: Prompting is steering a conversation. Grounding is constraining a decision engine, steering fails when the road is missing. Constraints hold even when the driver improvises.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable metaphor for why grounding architecture beats prompt training.

quotes.text: This is why permission trimming is performance tuning. Not just risk reduction. When you reduce overbroad access you don't only shrink blast radius. You reduce retrieval noise.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes permission cleanup as a quality lever for AI, not only a security chore.

quotes.text: Refusal is not a safety feature you bolt on later. Refusal is a design requirement for any system that will act, because probabilistic systems will always produce an answer.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States a core design rule for safe autonomous agents.

takeaways: Copilot is only an interaction surface; its reliability is bounded by the identity, permissions, memory and evidence in the tenant underneath it.

A reliable autonomy stack combines Microsoft Graph as memory, Dataverse as operational state, Fabric as the learning layer and Copilot as the interaction layer, with explicit relevance windows and refusal conditions.
Least privilege, continuous access evaluation and provenance are the guardrails that hold when context becomes an attack surface through prompt injection, memory poisoning and drift.
hook: Copilot rollouts often disappoint not because the model is weak but because enterprise context is fragmented, overshared and stale. This episode is for architects and Microsoft 365 leaders who want reliable Copilot and safe agents, and shows how to build context as architecture with Graph, Dataverse, Fabric and real guardrails.
